turn.user_message: ARPOB ₹8,000/day. ALOS 6.5 days. Average daily revenue ₹28 lakhs. Bed occupancy 89%, ICU 94%. OT utilisation 75%, daily OT revenue ₹5 lakhs.

transcript.label: Transcript turn 15 · dead bed time turned into money
transcript.said: That’s everything I needed. The graphic below turns your dead bed time into a revenue number, step by step, so you can check every line of the arithmetic rather than take it from me. Two things I’ve deliberately left out of it: an ALOS gain on top, because that would be the same bed-days counted twice; and OT, which needs more from you before it can be sized honestly. Last question before we move on: has anyone worked out what your admissions desk can actually handle per hour at peak — counting internal bed transfers alongside admissions — or is that team sized by habit?

text: The working turns your dead bed time into a revenue number, one line at a time. You can check every line rather than take it from me.
Two things I’ve left out on purpose. A shorter stay on top, because that would count the same days twice. And the operating theatre, which needs more from you first.
chat.invite: Last one before we move on. Has anyone worked out what your admissions desk can handle an hour at peak, bed transfers included?
chat.note: ₹1.5 to 2 crore a year, from your own figures.

options: Yes, we have worked it out
No, sized by habit and taken to be enough

blocks.title: From one bed to a year
blocks.deck: Every figure is yours. Move the hours won back between 3 and 4 to see the range.

blocks.beds_caption: Each bed sits 4 to 5 hours with no bill when it changes patient. The red line is that time.

readouts.label: Bed hours won back a year

blocks.caption: It holds only if freed hours are filled, and at 89% full they can. It uses the bed charge alone, so it understates.

sheets.title: Bed hours won back
sheets.text: 267 beds ÷ 6.5 days is about 41 changes a day. Each one wins back 3 to 4 hours, over 365 days.

lines.label: From
lines.value: Your beds, stay and dead bed time

sheets.title: Full days of bed time
sheets.text: The hours won back, divided by 24. About 1,900 to 2,500 bed days a year.

sheets.title: Revenue at stake
sheets.text: Those bed days at ₹8,000 each. Your ₹28 lakh a day suggests the ₹8,000 is the bed charge alone, so this is on the low side.

blocks.label: A shorter average stay
blocks.sub: A shorter stay frees the same days of bed time. Adding it on top would count them twice.
